decisions.reason: As a flagship new product line closely tied to the firm’s core software and digital-practice strategy, it is likely to stay on the market because an established R&D-active firm will tolerate early uncertainty unless results are clearly far below aspiration.

The education institute fits the installed customer base and support/training capabilities, so management would likely keep it while learning about demand, though it is somewhat more droppable because it is less central than the software core.

A remote screen-sharing support tool directly strengthens the firm’s existing service offering and customer relationships, so with normal organisational slack it would usually be retained unless early usage is clearly disappointing.
